surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Capitals take down the Devils
paras: Arseny Gritsyuk got the scoring started for the Devils midway through the first, but Ryan Leonard tied it 1-1 for Washington on the power play late in the period. Ilya Protas and Dylan Strome scored less than four minutes apart early in the second to put the Capitals up 3-1. Boone Jenner made it 4-1 midway through the period, but Timo Meier cut Washington’s lead to 4-2 on the power play with 19 seconds left.

The Devils had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Devils win about six in ten. Logan Thompson made the difference in net, stopping 29 of 31. Jake Allen stopped 21 of 25 for the Devils.
The Devils hit three posts, and the bounces never came. The Capitals improved to 5-3-0, and the Devils fell to 4-4-0.
